steps.cap: A chipmaking machine prints at most a patch 26 by 33 mm in one shot, about the size of a postage stamp, so no single chip can be bigger.
An AI accelerator needs more circuitry than one patch holds, so its logic is split into two chips, each nearly the size of a stamp.
The two chips sit side by side on a silicon base, called an interposer, whose fine wiring joins them.
Eight stacks of memory go beside them. Together the chips cover a little over three stamps of silicon.
The silicon base sits on a larger package base, the substrate. TSMC now builds silicon bases as large as five and a half stamps.
